cards.text: Friend, the prophet Hosea is in the middle of a hard message for Israel. He opens with a picture: “Israel was a luxuriant vine, yielding fruit for himself.” Picture it: Israel was THRIVING.

cards.question: But watch what happens as that vine grows. The more Israel's fruit increased, the more Israel increased the ___.
As Israel's land produced better, Israel made its sacred pillars better.

cards.text: Then Hosea says it plain: their hearts are devious, and now they must bear their guilt. Not confused, not having an off week. DEVIOUS.

cards.question: What does Hosea say the LORD will do to Israel's altars and sacred pillars?

cards.text: Next, Hosea tells what the people will say about having a king. And friend, it is NOT a pep rally.

cards.question: The people will say, “We have no king…” What reason will they give?

answers.text: We do not revere the LORD
The LORD has not sent one
We do not honor our elders

cards.question: Next, the people will say a king can do a lot for them.

cards.text: They speak mere words, and they make covenants with false oaths. It's like me telling a baker, 'I'll keep this story short,' and friend, I have NEVER kept a story short.

cards.question: All those false oaths grow into something. Judgment springs up like poisonous ___ in the furrows of a field.

cards.text: Now Hosea turns to the calf idol of Beth-aven, a place in Israel, and says the people of Samaria, a city of Israel, will fear for it. Friend, when your god needs YOU to do the worrying, something has gone sideways.

cards.question: The calf's people and its idolatrous priests will mourn over the calf of Beth-aven. Why?

answers.text: It has been taken into exile
It has been melted in a fire
It has been smashed by a prophet

cards.question: The calf of Beth-aven will be carried off to ___ as tribute to the great king.

cards.text: Then Hosea says Ephraim, one of Israel's tribes, will be seized with shame, and Israel will be ashamed of its wooden idols.

cards.question: Hosea says Samaria will be carried off, but her king will be left behind.

cards.text: Samaria will be carried off with her king, “like a twig on the surface of the water.” Just floating wherever the water says.
The high places of Aven will be destroyed, and Hosea calls it the sin of Israel. Thorns and thistles will overgrow their altars.

cards.question: Then the people will call out to the mountains and the hills. What will they ask for?

cards.text: Then Hosea reaches WAY back, to the days of Gibeah, a town in Israel.

cards.question: Hosea says Israel left its sin behind after the days of Gibeah.

cards.text: Hosea's words: “Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, O Israel, and there you have remained.” Friend, I spent YEARS stuck in a junk drawer, and even I think that's a long time to stay put.

cards.question: Hosea reminds Israel what overtook the sons of iniquity at Gibeah. What was it?

cards.text: Then the prophecy says, “I will chasten them when I please…” Not on Israel's schedule, friend.

cards.question: ___ will be gathered against Israel to put them in bondage for their double transgression.

cards.text: New picture: Ephraim is a well-trained heifer that loves to thresh. She LOVES her job, like me at the oven: nobody has to ask me twice, nobody has to ask me ONCE, I'm stamping cookies at three in the morning and NOBODY ordered any.

cards.question: Ephraim is a well-trained heifer that loves to thresh. But the prophecy says a ___ will be placed on her fair neck.
Next comes “I will harness Ephraim…” Then Judah, the southern kingdom, and Jacob, the man God renamed Israel (Genesis 32:28), will be put to work. Doing what?

cards.text: Then comes this: “Sow for yourselves righteousness and reap the fruit of loving devotion; break up your unplowed ground.” That's dough straight out of the fridge, friend: you can't roll out ANYTHING until you break it up first.

cards.question: Israel is told to break up the unplowed ground. Why now?

answers.text: It is time to seek the LORD
The ground will soon be sold

cards.question: Hosea pictures the LORD coming and sending righteousness upon them like ___.

cards.text: But here's what they actually did: they plowed wickedness, reaped injustice and ate the fruit of lies.

cards.question: Hosea says Israel trusted in their own way. What else did Israel trust in?

answers.text: The multitude of their mighty men

cards.text: Because of that, Hosea says the roar of battle will rise against Israel's people.

cards.question: Hosea says all of Israel's fortresses will be demolished.

cards.text: Hosea compares it to the day Shalman devastated a place called Beth-arbel, when mothers were dashed to pieces along with their children. I think this one hurts, friend.
Then the prophecy turns to Bethel, a town in Israel: “Thus it will be done to you, O Bethel, because of your great wickedness.”

cards.question: And when the day dawns, what will happen to the king of Israel?

answers.text: He will be utterly cut off
He will hide in the hills
